# 1 Enoch Chapter 26 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 26 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 26:1 — "the middle of the earth"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the middle of the earth" | Direct literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "the middle of the earth" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the center of the earth" | "Center" for "middle" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET "the middle of the earth." The traditional phrase in 1 Enoch scholarship and related literature is "middle/navel of the earth" — retaining "middle" preserves the technical cosmographic term better than PNEUMA's "center."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---

## 26:4 — "trees were not planted upon them" vs. "no trees were planted upon them"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "trees were not planted upon them" | Literal negation |
| LOGOS | "no trees were planted upon them" | Standard English negation |
| PNEUMA | "with no trees growing in them at all" | "Growing" rather than "planted"; "at all" emphatic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "no trees were planted upon them." "Planted" preserves the deliberate, cultivated nuance (the trees were absent by design or nature) rather than PNEUMA's "growing" which suggests merely botanical absence. LOGOS's negation is more natural than EMET's inversion.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 26:5 — Enoch's wonder

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I marveled very much" | Literal intensifier |
| LOGOS | "I marveled greatly" | Standard intensifier |
| PNEUMA | "I was utterly astonished" | Different verb; more dramatic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "I marveled greatly." The repetition of "I marveled" three times (vv. 5) is a Ge'ez literary device for emphasis; LOGOS preserves this structure with a final intensifier. PNEUMA's "utterly astonished" substitutes a different word and breaks the parallel.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 26:6 — "accursed valley" vs. "cursed valley"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "this accursed valley between" | "Accursed" — under a curse already placed |
| LOGOS | "this accursed valley between" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "that cursed valley lying between the mountains" | "Cursed" same meaning; adds "lying between the mountains" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET "this accursed valley between." "Accursed" (passive participle) emphasizes that the valley is under divine curse — slightly stronger than "cursed" (adjective). PNEUMA's addition "lying between the mountains" is redundant given the context.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---
